vocab.definition: Information about you that can be found online.
The people who can see or hear something.
Not for everyone to see or know.
An agreement to allow a specific action.
Another version of words or an image.
Check something before deciding what to do.
A version you can change before sharing.

cases.text: A photo shows a finished craft and a name badge on the table.
cases.fact: The badge could identify a person.
cases.next_step: Use a new photo of the craft with the badge and other private details removed.
cases.staff_note: Check the background, not just the main object. No actual badge is shown.

cases.text: A draft gives a home address so people can collect a project.
cases.fact: The draft exposes a private location.
cases.next_step: Remove the address; ask staff for the agreed safe collection route.
cases.staff_note: Do not ask pupils to write an actual address or arrange a collection.

cases.text: A post shows another person’s work. They have not agreed to share it.
cases.fact: Permission to share the work is not established.
cases.next_step: Ask before sharing; respect a no or no response.
cases.staff_note: Permission to share work does not make private details safe to include.

cases.text: A post says: I learnt to sort kit by label. It shows only the writer’s own work.
cases.fact: It can show a skill without names or private details.
cases.next_step: Check the claim is true, the background is clear and the audience fits.
cases.staff_note: Sharing useful work can be positive. Keeping it offline is also a valid choice.

cases.text: A post is for friends only. One friend makes a copy.
cases.fact: A viewer can make a copy beyond the first audience.
cases.next_step: Share less detail; ask a trusted adult for help if a copy causes worry.
cases.staff_note: Do not promise that deleting the original removes all copies.

cases.text: A message asks for a password to help improve a job profile.
cases.fact: A password gives access to an account.
cases.next_step: Do not send it. Ask a trusted adult through the agreed help route.
cases.staff_note: No real login, password, profile search or account access is needed.

Term theme: Identity & Belonging
We Do: 5 minutes.
Teacher: Read the hinge aloud, ask for a choice and a reason. B. A limited audience reduces exposure but cannot guarantee that a viewer will not copy or share content. A promises too much; C adds an unnecessary private detail. Ask what could be removed before sharing. If needed, model how a paper copy can leave its first audience, then recheck with a fictional group photo. Do not demonstrate on a real account.

Purpose and success checks
What might my posts show about me?
I can spot a detail that should stay private. I can choose who should see a post. I can give a reason for a safer change.

Before pupils arrive

Print the six fictional cards, evidence sheet and word mat. Use offline paper examples only. Identify the available support adult and safeguarding route. Do not ask learners to search for themselves or classmates, log in, show profiles or reveal private details.
Offer processing time, a quiet start and the usual communication support. Capture each learner’s own work. Read the Staff Answers before teaching.

Hinge and reteach

B. A limited audience reduces exposure but cannot guarantee that a viewer will not copy or share content. A promises too much; C adds an unnecessary private detail. Access and practice
Supported: choose one card and explain a step. Independent: review three posts and give reasons. Aspire: compare two safer ways to share work.

Use cards A, D and E as the three core reviews; the other cards extend discussion. Model A, then invite the learner to explain a choice using their own words. Safe teaching evidence and learner voice
Boundaries

Keep every example fictional and anonymous. Do not collect names, addresses, account handles, passwords or screenshots. Learners may pass on personal disclosure and use a card instead. If a concern arises, listen privately and follow the local safeguarding route; do not investigate it in the group. No account or post is changed in this lesson.
Assessment and feedback

Check the learner links a particular detail to a risk and chooses a proportionate action: keep after checks, edit, or do not share. Accept a supported review of one card and record that the other cards are not yet assessed. The rewritten post must avoid private details and include an audience check. A privacy setting is not proof that copying is impossible. Record the learner’s own explanation and revision, not just the adult model.

Retain actual work, response mode and support. Use VF · WS · I · NS+ (Yellow Box) · // (self-edit) · ? (read back) · R (responded) · E (evidence in the school’s evidence record). R requires Voice, Audience, an NS+ prompt and the learner’s response in their own colour. Record E only after evidence is banked. Blank forms and adult models are not completed learner evidence.
Learner voice
Space: calm, accessible participation. Voice: a choice, reason or help request. Audience: the adult listens or reads and replies. Influence: record the support or next-step change made in response.
Offer to the Communication portfolio

Explain a choice, listen to a different view and revise a short message for its audience. The receiving teacher maps authentic responses to their own portfolio; no communication criteria are assigned here.

Model and hinge

Made-up draft: a photo of a finished craft. A name badge is in the photo too. Pause: that badge shows a private detail. Use a new photo of just the craft. Check who can see it before sharing. A private setting does not stop all copies.

B. A limited audience reduces exposure but cannot guarantee that a viewer will not copy or share content. A promises too much; C adds an unnecessary private detail. Ask what could be removed before sharing. If needed, model how a paper copy can leave its first audience, then recheck with a fictional group photo. Do not demonstrate on a real account.
Individual evidence key

Check the learner links a particular detail to a risk and chooses a proportionate action: keep after checks, edit, or do not share. Accept a supported review of one card and record that the other cards are not yet assessed. The rewritten post must avoid private details and include an audience check. A privacy setting is not proof that copying is impossible. Record the learner’s own explanation and revision, not just the adult model.
Feedback boundaries and next teaching
Card A: Check the background, not just the main object. No actual badge is shown.
Card B: Do not ask pupils to write an actual address or arrange a collection.
Card C: Permission to share work does not make private details safe to include.
Card D: Sharing useful work can be positive. Keeping it offline is also a valid choice.
Card E: Do not promise that deleting the original removes all copies.
Card F: No real login, password, profile search or account access is needed.
Common misunderstandings

A digital footprint is more than the words you type: photos and others’ posts may also reveal details. Private settings limit an audience but do not guarantee secrecy. Removing a post may not remove copies. Positive, truthful work can be shared with care; no learner must publish anything.
Teaching boundary

Keep every example fictional and anonymous. Do not collect names, addresses, account handles, passwords or screenshots. Learners may pass on personal disclosure and use a card instead. If a concern arises, listen privately and follow the local safeguarding route; do not investigate it in the group. No account or post is changed in this lesson.
Feedback

If a reason is missing, return to the fact or actual work. Re-model a different example, then keep the learner’s own revision. Use NS+ and the learner response in their own colour before R. E means evidence actually banked. Keep safeguarding records separate.
